metadata.title: Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) misses practice Wednesday
metadata.description: Dontayvion Wicks did not participate in Wednesday's walkthrough practice.
metadata.analysis: Wicks was sidelined in Week 7 against the Cowboys. He'll need to be monitored in practice the rest of the week.

metadata.title: Dontayvion Wicks - DNP on Wednesday
metadata.description: Wicks (ankle) didn't take part in Wednesday's walkthrough.
metadata.analysis: Wicks thus has logged a DNP on four consecutive injury reports going back to last week as he deals with an ankle issue. He likely will need to practice in some capacity Thursday and/or Friday to have a chance to suit up Sunday at Washington.

metadata.title: Dontayvion Wicks is Absent from Wednesday's Walkthrough
metadata.description: Philadelphia Eagles wide receiver Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) was a non-participant during Wednesday's walkthrough, according to Zach Berman. Wicks sat out the Week 7 loss to the Dallas Cowboys, and him being absent start of this week isn't a great start. The expectation is that he'll need to at least participate in a limited capacity to have a chance to play against the Washington Commanders in Week 8. The Eagles are banged up at wide receiver with DeVonta Smith (hamstring) absent during Wednesday's walkthrough as well. Makai Lemon could end up being the top wideout again. Fantasy managers will need to check back throughout the week for more updates on Wicks and Smith ahead of Sunday's game.

metadata.title: Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) out for Week 7
metadata.description: Philadelphia Eagles wide receiver Dontayvion Wicks was ruled out for Monday Night Football against Dallas due to an ankle injury.
metadata.analysis: Wicks did not practice this week, so this does not come as a surprise. However, multiple important players will miss Week 7, including Wicks and wide receiver DeVonta Smith. Quarterback Tanner McKee will rely on a patchwork offense in a divisional matchup.

metadata.title: Dontayvion Wicks - Ruled out for Monday's game
metadata.description: Wicks (ankle) has been ruled out for Monday's game versus the Cowboys.
metadata.analysis: Wicks wasn't able to practice in any capacity during Week 7 prep due to an ankle injury and thus will miss his first contest of the campaign. With DeVonta Smith (hamstring) also sidelined Monday, the Eaglges will rely on a receiving corps composed of Makai Lemon, Darius Cooper, Hollywood Brown, Elijah Moore and Britain Covey, though TE Dallas Goedert (knee) may end being the favorite target of QB Tanner McKee.

metadata.title: Dontayvion Wicks - Not spotted at Saturday's practice
metadata.description: Wicks (ankle) was not on the field for the start of Saturday's practice, Andrew DiCecco of Inside the Birds reports.
metadata.analysis: It looks like both Wicks and DeVonta Smith (hamstring) will miss all three Week 7 practices, so the duo's chances of playing Monday against the Cowboys appears to be slim, but the Eagles will announce their injury designations following Saturday's session. Rookie Makai Lemon, Darius Cooper and tight end Dallas Goedert (knee) would all be involved more heavily in the offense if one or both of Wicks and Smith is sidelined.

metadata.title: Dontayvion Wicks Ruled Out for Week 7
metadata.description: Philadelphia Eagles wide receiver Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) has been ruled out for his team's Week 7 matchup against the Dallas Cowboys on Monday night. Wicks did not practice at all this week as he deals with an ankle injury. The 25-year-old has recorded 19 catches for 284 yards and a touchdown on 32 targets across six games this season and could have had a chance to be the Eagles' WR1 against Dallas. Instead, Philadelphia will be without both Wicks and star wideout DeVonta Smith (hamstring) on Monday night. The Eagles' injuries at wide receiver could open a path for rookie wideout Makai Lemon to assume a lead role in his team's passing game alongside tight end Dallas Goedert. Still, the overall health of the team's offense is a major question mark, with backup quarterback Tanner McKee set to make his second straight start in Week 7.

metadata.title: Dontayvion Wicks Remains Sidelined With Ankle Injury
metadata.description: Philadelphia Eagles wide receiver Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) is difficult to trust in fantasy lineups for Monday night's matchup against the Dallas Cowboys after missing Saturday's practice, his third consecutive absence, according to Jeff McLane of The Philadelphia Inquirer. He appeared positioned for more opportunities with DeVonta Smith (hamstring) also struggling to practice, but his own injury now threatens to keep him sidelined, and McLane previously indicated that Wicks was trending toward missing Monday's game. Wicks drew eight targets while Smith was absent in Week 5, catching five passes for 63 yards against the Jacksonville Jaguars. With Smith back and Tanner McKee starting in Week 6, he managed just two receptions for 24 yards on four targets against the Carolina Panthers, despite the potential opening in Philadelphia's receiving corps.

metadata.title: Dontayvion Wicks - Sits out Friday's practice
metadata.description: Wicks (ankle) didn't take part in Friday's practice.
metadata.analysis: With back-to-back DNPs to kick off Week 7 prep due to an ankle issue, Wicks has only one more opportunity to mix into drills Saturday before the Eagles potentially make a ruling on his status for Monday's contest against the Cowboys. Fellow WR DeVonta Smith (hamstring) also hasn't practiced this week, leaving Makai Lemon, Darius Cooper, Hollywood Brown, Elijah Moore and Britain Covey as the healthy options at the position on the active roster.

metadata.title: Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) absent from practice Friday
metadata.description: Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) was absent from Philadelphia's practice on Friday.
metadata.analysis: Wicks was not spotted at another practice session on Friday, which will mark the second-straight day that he has been a non-participant. His ankle injury may very well leave him sidelined this week, which would lead to more opportunities for rookie Makai Lemon against the Cowboys.

metadata.title: Dontayvion Wicks Trending in the Wrong Direction
metadata.description: Philadelphia Eagles wide receiver Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) was not spotted at Friday's practice ahead of Monday night's Week 7 matchup against the Dallas Cowboys, according to Jeff McLane of The Philadelphia Inquirer. He sat out Thursday too, coming off two catches for 24 yards on four targets against the Carolina Panthers in Week 6. That follows 19 receptions for 284 yards and one touchdown through six games, a modest line for a receiver who may not have a status until after most fantasy lineups lock. DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dallas Goedert (knee) have also missed both practices this week, so Philadelphia's receiving group is short-handed. Saturday's practice status will matter, but even if Wicks plays, he is hard to trust. McLane also said that he got the sense that Wicks would not be available to play on Monday night against the Cowboys.

metadata.title: Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) sidelined at practice Thursday
metadata.description: Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) was sidelined at practice on Thursday.
metadata.analysis: The young wideout wasn't able to practice on Thursday, as he's managing an ankle issue of some kind right now. It could threaten his availability for Week 7, but only if he's not able to practice on Friday either.

metadata.title: Dontayvion Wicks - DNP due to ankle injury
metadata.description: Wicks (ankle) was a non-participant at Thursday's practice.
metadata.analysis: Wicks made a very brief exit late in this past Sunday's loss to the Panthers but was able to return. With an ankle injury being cited as the reason for Thursday's absence, the nature of the injury has been revealed. Both Wicks and No. 1 WR DeVonta Smith (hamstring) were DNPs to kick off Week 7 prep, so the situation bears watching to see if either of them will be able to play Monday against the Cowboys.

metadata.title: Dontayvion Wicks Dealing With Ankle Injury, Misses Practice
metadata.description: Philadelphia Eagles wide receiver Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) was listed as a non-participant in the first practice of the week on Thursday, according to Jeff McLane of The Philadelphia Inquirer. Top Eagles receiver DeVonta Smith (hamstring) was also a non-participant, so the Eagles could be down two of their top receivers for a Monday night matchup against the division-rival Dallas Cowboys in Week 7 if they do not return to practice in the next two days. The 25-year-old injured his ankle late in the Week 6 loss to the Carolina Panthers, but he was able to return to the game, which gives some hope that he will be available to play on Monday night. Wicks has stepped up as Philly's WR2 behind Smith in his first year with the team, catching 19 of his 32 targets for 284 yards and one touchdown through six games. However, his fantasy value as a deep-league flex play diminished when it was announced earlier this week that star quarterback Jalen Hurts (blood clots) would miss the rest of the season. Fantasy managers should look to avoid Wicks if he is trending as a game-time decision for Monday's contest. He caught just two of four targets for 24 yards with backup Tanner McKee running the offense.

metadata.title: Dontayvion Wicks - Not spotted Thursday
metadata.description: Wicks was not spotted during the portion of Thursday's practice open to the media, Jimmy Kempski of The Philly Voice reports.
metadata.analysis: The Eagles are holding a few key pass catchers out of practice Thursday, including Wicks, DeVonta Smith and Dallas Goedert. It could just be a rest day for those players, with clarification on any potential injuries to come on Thursday's injury report. If Wicks is dealing with an injury, he'll have an extra day to recover since the Eagles play Monday against Dallas.

metadata.title: Dontayvion Wicks' Targets Drop With Eagles Receiving Corps Healthier
metadata.description: Philadelphia Eagles wide receiver Dontayvion Wicks saw his opportunities shrink in Sunday's 25-14 loss to the Carolina Panthers, catching just two of four targets for 24 yards after drawing eight targets in Week 5. The return of DeVonta Smith, who missed the previous two games, reshaped Philadelphia's receiving hierarchy. Smith caught seven passes for 75 yards and a touchdown, while Dallas Goedert added six receptions for 61 yards. Wicks briefly visited the medical tent during the fourth quarter before returning, though the nature of the injury remains unclear. He now has 19 catches for 284 yards and one touchdown through six games, and his weekly outlook is further clouded by Jalen Hurts' expected season-long absence. Tanner McKee threw for 215 yards in his first start of 2026, and the uncertainty around Philadelphia's passing offense makes Wicks hard to trust as an immediate fantasy starter. Rostered in 33% of leagues, he's a speculative addition in 12-team formats ahead of Monday's Week 7 matchup against Dallas.

metadata.title: Dontayvion Wicks - Only two catches vs. Carolina
metadata.description: Wicks caught two of four passes for 24 yards during the Eagles' 25-14 loss to the Panthers on Sunday.
metadata.analysis: Wicks' 24 receiving yards were his second-lowest of the season, but he still finished third among Eagles pass catchers in that category Sunday behind DeVonta Smith (75) and Dallas Goedert (61). Week 6 was the Eagles' first game with Tanner McKee under center, and with Jalen Hurts (calf) out for the rest of the season, the scoring floors of Wicks and the other Philadelphia pass catchers figure to be lower moving forward. That said, the Eagles have a juicy Week 7 matchup on Monday, Oct. 26 against the Cowboys, whose defense ranks in the bottom-10 in the league in fantasy points allowed per game to wide receivers.

metadata.title: Dontayvion Wicks catches two passes in Week 6
metadata.description: Philadelphia Eagles wide receiver Dontayvion Wicks caught two passes for 24 yards in Week 6 against the Carolina Panthers.
metadata.analysis: Wicks had a quiet day after his eight-target outing against Jacksonville in London in Week 5. His four targets were more in line with his season average - he has earned 4-5 in four of six games - but he had a season low in yardage. With Jalen Hurts sidelined, Wicks' role could change going forward.

metadata.title: Dontayvion Wicks - Returns Sunday
metadata.description: Wicks (undisclosed) returned to Sunday's contest versus the Panthers, Brooks Kubena of The Athletic reports.
metadata.analysis: Both Wicks and fellow WR Makai Lemon (undisclosed) visited the medial tent in the second half, but both of them were able to rejoin Week 6 action.

metadata.title: Dontayvion Wicks - Exits Sunday's game
metadata.description: Wicks (undisclosed) went to the medical tent during Sunday's game versus the Panthers, Brooks Kubena of The Athletic reports.
metadata.analysis: Wicks was tripped up by a Panthers defender at the end of a catch and run in the fourth quarter, and he went down to the turf before going to the sideline. He had two catches (on four targets) for 24 yards before his departure.

metadata.title: Dontayvion Wicks - Clear for Week 6
metadata.description: Wicks (hamstring) doesn't have a designation for Sunday's contest versus the Panthers.
metadata.analysis: Wicks was limited Wednesday and didn't log any on-field work Thursday, but an uncapped session Friday has him in the clear for Week 6 action. He'll be welcoming back DeVonta Smith (hamstring) to the lineup, though, which may not allow Wicks to reach the 6.5 targets per game that he received during Smith's two-game absence.

metadata.title: Dontayvion Wicks (hamstring) off injury report Sunday
metadata.description: Dontayvion Wicks is off the injury report for Sunday's game against the Panthers.
metadata.analysis: Wicks returned to a full practice on Friday after he missed practice on Thursday.

metadata.title: Dontayvion Wicks Leads Eagles in Receiving Yards Entering Week 6
metadata.description: Wide receiver Dontayvion Wicks (hamstring) has essentially operated as the No. 1 wide receiver for the Philadelphia Eagles with DeVonta Smith (hamstring) missing the past two games with a hamstring injury. In Week 5 against the Jacksonville Jaguars, Wicks saw eight targets, which was the second-most on the team behind tight end Dallas Goedert. Wicks turned those opportunities into five receptions for 63 yards (12.6 yards per catch), but he did not find the end zone. Only Darius Cooper (71 yards on two receptions) had more receiving yards for the Eagles against the Jaguars. Now, Wicks and the Eagles return to Philadelphia for a Week 6 matchup with the Carolina Panthers. Wicks has been dealing with a hamstring injury, and he missed Thursday's practice this week, but he played through it against Jacksonville last week and is expected to play against the Panthers as well. Smith is returning in Week 6, but Wicks should still be involved against Carolina as the No. 2 wideout for the Eagles. The big question mark for Wicks and the wide receivers, though, is how well backup quarterback Tanner McKee will play in place of Jalen Hurts (calf). The Panthers currently allow 230.8 passing yards per game (22nd in the NFL). However, Carolina is one of the stingier teams in the league when it comes to allowing fantasy points to wide receivers. According to Pro Football Reference, the Panthers rank fourth in the NFL, allowing 16.2 fantasy points per game to wideouts. Wicks currently leads the Eagles with 260 receiving yards, and he has scored one touchdown. His 17 receptions rank second on the team, behind Smith's 19, and Wicks is averaging 15.3 yards per reception. He is RotoBaller's No. 41 wide receiver (half-PPR) for Week 6 and is projected to score 7.1 fantasy points. Wicks has flex or possibly WR3 fantasy appeal.

metadata.title: Dontayvion Wicks - Returns to practice Friday
metadata.description: Wicks (hamstring) is practicing Friday, Andrew DiCecco reports.
metadata.analysis: The extent of Wicks' participation is unclear, but it's at least a good sign relative to Thursday when he didn't practice at all. He was limited Wednesday, after playing through the injury in a Week 5 loss to Jacksonville. Fellow Eagle wideout DeVonta Smith (hamstring) also returned to practice Thursday, but it isn't clear if he has a real shot to play Sunday against the Panthers.

metadata.title: Dontayvion Wicks (hamstring) doesn't practice Thursday
metadata.description: Dontayvion Wicks (hamstring) did not take part in Philadelphia's practice on Thursday.
metadata.analysis: Wicks was not able to practice on Thursday. He's managing some kind of a hamstring issue and seems to be trending the wrong way for Week 6. Look for rookie Makai Lemon to see more work if Wicks is out this week, although neither of them should be started in this matchup against the Panthers either way.

metadata.title: Dontayvion Wicks - Doesn't practice Thursday
metadata.description: Wicks (hamstring) didn't practice Thursday, Zach Berman of The Athletic reports.
metadata.analysis: Wicks was limited on the final two Week 5 injury reports due to a hamstring issue, but he didn't carry a designation into the weekend and suited up for this past Sunday's loss to the Jaguars in London, earning an 84 percent snap share and hauling in five of eight targets for 63 yards. He opened this week as limited Wednesday, so his downgrade one day later may be cause for concern. Friday's practice report could unveil if Wicks is in danger of missing Sunday's contest against the Panthers.

metadata.title: Dontayvion Wicks (hamstring) limited in practice Wednesday
metadata.description: Dontayvion Wicks was limited in practice on Wednesday.
metadata.analysis: Wicks is on the injury report with a hamstring issue. He should be good to go for Sunday's game against the Panthers.

metadata.title: Dontayvion Wicks - Limited Wednesday
metadata.description: Wicks (hamstring) practiced in a limited capacity Wednesday.
metadata.analysis: Wicks now has been listed as limited on three consecutive injury reports dating back to last week due to a hamstring issue, but he wasn't tagged with a designation for a Week 5 matchup with the Jaguars in London. He ended up earning an 84 percent snap share in that contest, which he parlayed into five catches (on eight targets) for 63 yards with top WR DeVonta Smith (hamstring) out for a second game in a row. Wicks doesn't appear to be in danger of sitting out this Sunday versus the Panthers, but his status nonetheless will be monitored as the week goes on.

metadata.title: Dontayvion Wicks a Worthy Deep Flex Option
metadata.description: Philadelphia Eagles wide receiver Dontayvion Wicks is gaining value after a solid performance against the Jacksonville Jaguars this past weekend. The Eagles were without top wideout DoVonta Smith (hamstring), so Wicks stepped up as the top option in Week 5. The 25-year-old hauled in five of his eight targets for 63 yards in the loss. Wicks has posted good performances this season, including two 70-plus yard games, but his value will take a hit once Smith is back. Wicks should be put in the deep league flex conversation for Week 6. He appears to have earned himself more opportunities in Philly.

metadata.title: Dontayvion Wicks - Five receptions in loss
metadata.description: Wicks caught five of eight targets for 63 yards during Sunday's 19-17 loss to the Jaguars.
metadata.analysis: Wicks led the team in targets, and he was able to match his season-high five catches in the defeat. The wide receiver also exceeded 60 receiving yards for the third time this season and first time since Week 2. Wicks has now caught 17 of 28 targets for 260 yards and a touchdown over his first five regular-season contests as a member of the Eagles.

metadata.title: Dontayvion Wicks hauls in five passes Sunday
metadata.description: Dontayvion Wicks secured 5-of-8 targets for 63 yards in Sunday's 19-17 loss to the Jaguars.
metadata.analysis: With top wideout DeVonta Smith (hamstring) out for the second straight week, Wicks saw a season high in targets Sunday. He also tied a season high with five receptions and crossed the 60-yard mark for the third time in the first five weeks. Wicks is at least in the flex conversation for standard leagues right now.

metadata.title: Dontayvion Wicks (hamstring) off injury report Sunday
metadata.description: Dontayvion Wicks is off the injury report for Sunday's game against the Jaguars.
metadata.analysis: Wicks will be good to go despite being added to the injury report on Thursday. He'll be a WR3 for fantasy managers.

metadata.title: Dontayvion Wicks - Good to go Sunday
metadata.description: Wicks (hamstring) doesn't carry an injury designation into Sunday's game against the Jaguars.
metadata.analysis: With DeVonta Smith (hamstring) set to miss a second straight contest, Wicks, Makai Lemon and Darius Cooper should comprise Philly's three-wide set against Jacksonville. Wicks paced the group in snaps and routes last Sunday against the Rams and saw five targets.

metadata.title: Dontayvion Wicks Hoping for More Production Vs. Jaguars
metadata.description: Wide receiver Dontayvion Wicks (hamstring) entered the Week 4 matchup versus the Los Angeles Rams as the Philadelphia Eagles' de facto No. 1 wide receiver, but the results were disappointing in the 24-20 loss. With leading wide receiver DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and tight end Dallas Goedert (knee) both missing the contest against the Rams due to injury, and running back Saquon Barkley (hamstring) exiting the game in the first quarter with a hamstring injury, Wicks had the opportunity for a productive day, but that was not the case. Wicks saw five targets on the day, but he tallied just three receptions for 18 yards (6.0 yards per reception) and did not score. Wicks was behind both Darius Cooper (seven) and rookie Makai Lemon (six) in targets, although each player recorded three receptions. Cooper amassed 33 receiving yards and two touchdowns, while Lemon totaled 27 receiving yards. Wicks is dealing with a hamstring injury this week, but is expected to play against the Jaguars. He will look for a better performance against the Jacksonville Jaguars in London in Week 5. Philadelphia will be without Smith, Barkley and others, giving Wicks another opportunity to be heavily involved. The good news for Wicks is that Jacksonville allows the second-most passing yards in the NFL, giving up 280.3 yards per game through the air. The bad news for Wicks and the Eagles is the Jaguars rank in the top-three in the NFL in scoring defense (13.3 points per game) and are among the very best teams in the league at forcing turnovers. Through four games in 2026, Wicks has caught 12 passes for 197 yards (16.4 yards per reception) and a touchdown. He is RotoBaller's No. 30 wide receiver for Week 4 and is projected to score 7.8 fantasy points. While he should see targets against the Jags, Wicks is a touchdown-dependent boom-or-bust candidate for Week 5.

metadata.title: Dontayvion Wicks Cleared for Week 5 Despite Hamstring Injury
metadata.description: Philadelphia Eagles wide receiver Dontayvion Wicks (hamstring) was limited in practice Friday but carries no injury designation into Sunday's game against Jacksonville in London. Wicks suffered the injury during Thursday's session, briefly putting his availability in question. With DeVonta Smith (hamstring) ruled out, Wicks should have an opportunity for more targets, although he didn't do much with an expanded role against the Rams last week. He caught just three of five targets for 18 yards in that game and has 12 receptions for 197 yards and a touchdown through four contests. Dallas Goedert (knee) is also returning after missing the past two games, giving Jalen Hurts another established receiving option. Wicks should see opportunities with Smith sidelined, but his recent production makes him a risky flex play despite being cleared for Sunday.

metadata.title: Dontayvion Wicks (hamstring) expected to practice Friday
metadata.description: Eagles coach Nick Sirianni said he expects Dontayvion Wicks to practice on Friday.
metadata.analysis: Wicks was added to the injury report on Friday with a hamstring issue. A practice of any kind on Friday is a good sign for his availability heading into Sunday.

metadata.title: Dontayvion Wicks - On track to practice Friday
metadata.description: Head coach Nick Sirianni anticipates that Wicks (hamstring) "will be out there" at Friday's practice, according to the Eagles' official X account.
metadata.analysis: Sirianni confirmed that Wicks injured his hamstring during Thursday's session, and he wound up as a limited participant on the injury report. While it appears Wicks will get some work in Friday, his status for Week 5 will not be known until the Eagles release their final injury report of the week following Friday's practice.

metadata.title: Dontayvion Wicks - Limited by hamstring issue
metadata.description: Wicks was limited at Thursday's practice due to a hamstring injury, Jeff McLane of The Philadelphia Inquirer reports.
metadata.analysis: Wicks' addition to the injury report midweek indicates that he may have picked up the health concern at practice, but he joins DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Hollywood Brown (ankle) as banged-up players at the position. Currently, rookie first-rounder Makai Lemon, Darius Cooper, Elijah Moore and Britain Covey are the Eagles' healthy wide receivers.

metadata.title: Dontayvion Wicks Added to Injury Report With Hamstring Injury
metadata.description: Philadelphia Eagles wide receiver Dontayvion Wicks (hamstring) was added to the team's injury report with a hamstring injury on Thursday, according to Jeff McLane of The Philadelphia Inquirer. Wicks was limited in practice, which suggests he suffered the injury on Thursday after he was a full participant on Wednesday. Top wideout DeVonta Smith (hamstring) missed last week's loss to the Los Angeles Rams on Sunday and has not practiced yet this week, although he was seen getting some running in on a side rehab field on Thursday. With both of Philly's top pass-catchers questionable to play in London on Sunday against the Jacksonville Jaguars, rookie first-rounder Makai Lemon could be thrust into a big pass-catching role in a tough matchup this weekend. Veteran Hollywood Brown (ankle) is also banged up, so alongside Lemon, Darius Cooper could have an expanded role as the Eagles look to bounce back against another tough opponent. If the 25-year-old Wicks ends up suiting up this weekend and Smith sits a second straight game, he should have a much better game than his three-catch, 18-yard performance against the Rams with Smith out last weekend. Wicks had 147 receiving yards and a touchdown in the first two weeks of the season but has produced just five catches for 50 yards in the last two games.

metadata.title: Eagles Injuries Could Set Dontayvion Wicks Up for Major Role
metadata.description: Philadelphia Eagles wide receiver Dontayvion Wicks should see an expanded role in the offense with DeVonta Smith (hamstring) sidelined. In Week 4, Wicks caught just three of five targets for 18 yards in the 24-20 loss to the Los Angeles Rams, facing a tough matchup against cornerback Trent McDuffie. Despite the off game, he played 56 of 61 snaps (92%) and ran 31 of 32 routes (97%). With injuries to running backs Saquon Barkley (hamstring) and Tank Bigsby (core), along with Smith and tight end Dallas Goedert (knee), Wicks may be the only target left in this depleted offense. He faces the Jacksonville Jaguars' defense in London, which has allowed the most receiving yards to wide receivers in 2026, including big games for Tee Higgins and Jaylen Waddle in two of the last three weeks. Given the Eagles' significant number of offensive injuries, Wicks could be a strong FLEX play in Week 5 and should be rostered in all formats.

metadata.title: Dontayvion Wicks - Three catches in loss
metadata.description: Wicks caught three of five targets for 18 yards during Sunday's 24-20 loss to the Rams.
metadata.analysis: Wicks was slated to operate as the team's No. 1 wide receiver in Week 4 with DeVonta Smith (hamstring) sidelined. He finished third on the team in targets behind fellow wideouts Darius Cooper (7) and Makai Lemon (6), while his 18 receiving yards were a season low. Wicks will have an easier matchup in Week 5 against the Jaguars, regardless of whether Smith is available or not.

metadata.title: Dontayvion Wicks disappoints in loss Sunday
metadata.description: Dontayvion Wicks caught 3-of-5 targets for just 18 yards in Sunday's 24-20 loss to the Los Angeles Rams.
metadata.analysis: Wicks wasn't able to get much going on Sunday. He finished with just 18 yards through the air against the Rams, which of course left him with a poor fantasy total. He should bounce back sometime in the near future, though a big part of his outlook will also depend on the health of Devonta Smith (hamstring) moving forward.

metadata.title: Dontayvion Wicks Falls Flat in Favorable Spot
metadata.description: Philadelphia Eagles wide receiver Dontayvion Wicks recorded three catches and 18 yards on five targets in the team's 24-20 home loss to the Los Angeles Rams. Philly's offense struggled on Sunday, totaling 172 yards. It's no surprise, really, considering they were down four starters before the game began. Still, the attack couldn't get anything going after halftime, and no Eagles pass catcher recorded more than three receptions or 33 yards. Wicks' target share has been favorable -- acting as the second option at worst behind teammate DeVonta Smith (hamstring). Moreover, he'll get plenty of opportunities while Smith and tight end Dallas Goedert (knee) are shelved. However, with quarterback Jalen Hurts' erratic play, it's challenging to project Wicks for a reliable weekly floor. He'll get a dream matchup in a porous Jaguars pass defense next weekend in London.

metadata.title: Dontayvion Wicks To See WR1 Role For Week 4 vs Rams
metadata.description: Philadelphia Eagles wide receiver Dontayvion Wicks will see an expanded role with his offense in Week 4, as Eagles WR1 DeVonta Smith (hamstring) has been ruled out with a hamstring injury for the game. Smith was targeted 27 times across the team's first three contests, meaning there's a significant target vacuum to be spread around to the team's other players. Additionally, Eagles TE1 Dallas Goedert (knee) won't be able to suit up for this contest, meaning Wicks could see heavy target volume. The Rams are one of the NFL's best offenses, and could force Philly into a pass-heavy game script. The matchup is a bit tough for Wicks, though -- the former Packer will face off with cornerback Trent McDuffie on the outside, though opposite-side starting CB Jaylen Watson (shoulder) has been ruled out for the game. Wicks is anything but a guaranteed high scorer, but he can be started as a low-end WR2 based on projected volume alone.

metadata.title: Dontayvion Wicks - Philly's WR1 for Week 4
metadata.description: Wicks will operate as the top wide receiver against the Rams on Sunday due to the absence of DeVonta Smith (hamstring), Chris McPherson of the Eagles' official site reports.
metadata.analysis: Wicks has the second-most targets, catches and receiving yards on the Eagles behind Smith through the first three games of the regular season. Smith gutted through a hamstring injury against the Bears in Week 3, but the star wide receiver will observe Sunday's game from the sidelines, meaning Wicks, rookie first-rounder Makai Lemon and Darius Cooper are all in line for more offensive snaps and targets from Jalen Hurts.

metadata.title: Dontayvion Wicks - Held quiet in Week 3 loss
metadata.description: Wicks recorded two receptions for 32 yards on five targets in Monday's 27-7 loss to the Bears.
metadata.analysis: Though he didn't find paydirt, Wicks played a critical role on the Eagles' lone scoring drive on the night late in the second quarter, leading off the possession with a 13-yard catch and run. He was otherwise held in check while the game was still competitive, with his lone other reception coming with 6:30 remaining, when the Bears had built a 20-point lead. Through his first three games with Philadelphia, Wicks has produced a 9-179-1 receiving line on 15 targets.

metadata.title: Dontayvion Wicks Remains a Must-Add Wide Receiver Despite Quiet Week 3
metadata.description: Across three games so far in 2026, Philadelphia Eagles wide receiver Dontayvion Wicks has recorded nine catches for 179 yards and a touchdown on 15 targets. Like the rest of the Eagles offense, Wicks had a frustrating game in his team's Week 3 loss to the Chicago Bears, recording just two catches for 30 yards. However, he topped 70 receiving yards in each of the Eagles' first two games and is averaging five targets per contest. Perhaps most importantly for fantasy managers, Wicks has been on the field for 78% of Philadelphia's offensive snaps this season and profiles as the team's WR2 alongside DeVonta Smith. With Eagles tight end Dallas Goedert (knee) currently sidelined by a knee injury, Wicks could be the number two option in the Philly passing game for the next several weeks. In leagues where he's not already rostered, Wicks profiles as a priority waiver wire target for fantasy managers.

metadata.title: Dontayvion Wicks draws five targets in Week 3
metadata.description: Dontayvion Wicks caught two of his five targets for 32 yards in a 27-7 loss to the Bears in Week 3.
metadata.analysis: Wicks finished second on the team in receiving yards on a rough evening for the Philly passing attack. The veteran wideout has been solid for the Eagles thus far, catching nine passes for 179 yards and a touchdown through three games. He will be a flex option in fantasy heading into Week 4 against the Rams.

metadata.title: Dontayvion Wicks Has Flex Appeal in Week 3
metadata.description: Philadelphia Eagles wide receiver Dontayvion Wicks has made enough plays through two weeks to stay in the flex conversation against Chicago. He has seven catches for 147 yards and a touchdown, including five receptions for 74 yards on six targets against Tennessee last week. The volume still is not especially heavy, and Wicks lost some snaps to Darius Cooper late in that game, so there is some risk in assuming the early production continues at the same pace. DeVonta Smith (hamstring) is available for Monday night, while Dallas Goedert (knee) and Hollywood Brown (ankle) have been ruled out. That leaves Wicks with a reasonable path to another useful game without making him a player fantasy managers have to force into lineups. He sits at WR36 in RotoBaller's Week 3 PPR rankings. Wicks makes sense as a flex option in deeper formats, while managers with a steadier choice can reasonably leave him on the bench.

metadata.title: Can Dontayvion Wicks Keep Up His Strong Start Against the Bears?
metadata.description: Philadelphia Eagles wide receiver Dontayvion Wicks is off to a good start in 2026. He works as Philadelphia's No. 2 wide receiver and has accumulated seven receptions for 147 yards (21.0 yards per catch) and a touchdown. While he isn't necessarily a PPR machine, Wicks has shown the ability to make big plays. He recorded two receptions for 74 yards and a score - including a 64-yard catch and a nine-yard touchdown play - in Week 1 against the Washington Commanders. He followed that up with a five-catch, 74-yard performance, including a 27-yard reception, against the Tennessee Titans in Week 2. Now, Wicks will see a Monday Night Football matchup with a Chicago Bears team that is allowing 240 net passing yards per game. He currently ranks as a top-18 wide receiver in half-PPR leagues and is averaging 3.46 fantasy points per touch. While Wicks does lag behind in targets (10) to fellow wide receiver DeVonta Smith (19), he could see even more opportunities in the passing game this week with tight end Dallas Goedert out. Currently rostered in 47% of Yahoo leagues - a 19% increase week-over-week - Wicks could be a solid streaming option in what looks to be a good matchup against the Bears. Wicks ranks as RotoBaller's No. 35 wide receiver for Week 3 and is projected to score 8.1 fantasy points.

metadata.title: Dontayvion Wicks Makes a Solid WR Addition in All Formats
metadata.description: Philadelphia Eagles wide receiver Dontayvion Wicks has gotten off to a strong start to the season with his new team, and he is a very solid pickup from the waiver wire as he continues to settle into his new offense. In Week 1, he showed his big-play ability and finished with two catches for 73 yards and a touchdown. He didn't find the end zone in Week 2, but he was more involved overall, hauling in five of his six targets for 74 yards against the Titans. Wicks did lose some snaps to Darius Cooper down the stretch, but as long as he remains the second option at receiver behind DeVonta Smith, he'll be a very viable fantasy option in most leagues. Dallas Goedert (knee) is expected to miss a few weeks, which could open up a few more targets for Wicks. This week, the Eagles visit the Bears on Monday Night Football, and Wicks will be a deep-league WR4 play with a high ceiling due to his big-play upside. For shallow leagues, he's not quite a starter yet, but he is a solid depth pickup in all formats.

metadata.title: Dontayvion Wicks - Five catches in win over Tennessee
metadata.description: Wicks caught five of six targets for 74 yards in Sunday's 24-20 win over the Titans.
metadata.analysis: While he wasn't able to get into the end zone, Wicks still had a strong showing as the Eagles' clear WR2 behind DeVonta Smith and ahead of rookie first-round pick Makai Lemon. The former Packer is looking good in his new offense, producing a 7-147-1 line on 10 targets through two contests, and Wicks will look to keep developing chemistry with Jalen Hurts in a Week 3 road trip to Chicago.

metadata.title: Dontayvion Wicks goes for 74 yards in Week 2
metadata.description: Dontayvion Wicks caught five of his six targets for 74 yards in a 24-20 win over the Titans in Week 2.
metadata.analysis: Wicks finished second on the Eagles in all receiving categories in the close win. The veteran wideout could stay involved as the Eagles lost Dallas Goedert to a knee injury in the game. Wicks is on the radar as a flex option in fantasy heading into Week 3 against the Bears.

metadata.title: Dontayvion Wicks finds end zone in Week 1 win
metadata.description: Dontayvion Wicks hauled in two of his four targets for 73 yards and one touchdown in the Eagles' 24-22 Week 1 win over the Washington Commanders.
metadata.analysis: Wicks made the most of his modest target share in the season opener, averaging 36.5 yards per reception in the win. The wideout offers head coach Nick Sirianni another explosive pass-catching option moving forward, with a favorable Week 2 matchup against the Tennessee Titans up next.

metadata.title: Dontayvion Wicks Worth Adding After Explosive Eagles Debut
metadata.description: Philadelphia Eagles wide receiver Dontayvion Wicks made two catches count in Sunday's 24-22 win over Washington, finishing with 73 yards and a touchdown on four targets. His first reception as an Eagle went 64 yards, and he later got loose from Mike Sainristil for a nine-yard score. That kind of stat line can be easy to dismiss on only four looks, but Wicks wasn't coming from nowhere. He started Week 1, remains listed with the first team on Philadelphia's depth chart, and the Eagles traded a 2026 fifth-round pick and 2027 sixth-rounder for him before extending him through 2027. Philadelphia also threw just 25 times in the opener. Four targets are the part to watch. That is not enough to call Wicks a weekly starter with DeVonta Smith, Dallas Goedert and first-round rookie Makai Lemon all competing for the ball. There is a real role here, though, plus enough downfield ability to matter without huge volume. Wicks is worth adding in 12-team leagues before Week 2 at Tennessee, especially for managers looking for receiver upside rather than an immediate plug-and-play option.

metadata.title: Dontayvion Wicks - Hauls in TD in Philly debut
metadata.description: Wicks caught two of four targets for 73 yards and a touchdown Sunday in a 24-22 Week 1 victory against Washington.
metadata.analysis: Wicks didn't log a particularly high volume of targets, but he nonetheless put up a nice fantasy score thanks to a 64-yard connection with Jalen Hurts late in the first quarter and a nine-yard TD catch in the second. Hurts spread the ball around pretty evenly, hooking up with six different pass catchers, none of whom logged more than four receptions. It could play into Wicks' favor if the Eagles' new offense encourages Hurts to spread the ball around, though all of DeVonta Smith, Makai Lemon and tight end Dallas Goedert figure to need to be fed in addition to Wicks.

metadata.title: Dontayvion Wicks - Listed as starting WR on depth chart
metadata.description: Wicks is listed as a starter on the Eagles' unofficial depth chart.
metadata.analysis: Philadelphia lists three starting wide receivers, with those spots going to Wicks, DeVonta Smith and rookie first-round pick Makai Lemon. Wicks had 581 receiving yards as a rookie with the Packers during the 2023 regular season and has failed to reach that mark since, posting only 415 receiving yards in the 2024 regular season and 332 yards in 2025. The 25-year-old wide receiver has an opportunity to play a larger role with his new team, which will kick off regular-season action Sunday against the Commanders.

metadata.title: Dontayvion Wicks Is a Potential Waiver-Wire Pickup
metadata.description: Philadelphia Eagles wide receiver Dontayvion Wicks is a nice addition to the Eagles receiving corps coming from the Green Bay Packers, and he could challenge for the No. 2 receiver role in Philadelphia. He could also emerge as a popular early-season waiver wire pickup. The Eagles drafted Makai Lemon out of USC, but he might fit in more as a slot receiver with Wicks playing on the outside. Last year in Green Bay, Wicks was in a room full of talented receivers, but he did finish the season with 46 targets and 30 catches for 332 yards and two touchdowns. Reuben Frank of NBC Sports Philadelphia wrote that Wicks could expand his role in Philadelphia to more than a role player. He quoted Eagles wide receivers coach Aaron Moorehead: "There's nothing that should be holding him back from anything in this league. He can go out here and have as good a year as anybody. Exciting time for him to prove that, 'Hey, I can be more than what I was in Green Bay.'"

metadata.title: Dontayvion Wicks Set for Starting Role in Philadelphia
metadata.description: Philadelphia Eagles wide receiver Dontayvion Wicks is expected to occupy a starting role when the regular season gets underway next week. Wicks was traded from the Packers to the Eagles this offseason, and he'll immediately occupy a significant role following the departure of A.J. Brown. All signs point to the 25-year-old opening the regular season as Philly's No. 2 receiver, starting opposite DeVonta Smith. His track record in Green Bay was iffy, but there was never any doubt about his role with the Eagles. After all, he was held out of all three preseason games due to his status as a projected starter. We expect the Eagles' offense to trend upward under new offensive coordinator Sean Mannion, which bodes well for Wicks' upside as a low-end WR3/flex. For now, he's an extremely affordable option in fantasy drafts. The latest ADP has him as a fringe draft pick in 12-team leagues and a 14th-round pick in 14-team leagues.

metadata.title: Dontayvion Wicks Set to Open Season as Eagles' WR2
metadata.description: Philadelphia Eagles wide receiver Dontayvion Wicks is expected to open the season as the team's No. 2 option behind DeVonta Smith, according to Jimmy Kempski of PhillyVoice. Kempski called the battle for Wicks earlier in camp, and that read hasn't changed with first-round rookie Makai Lemon back as a full participant. Wicks has earned consistent praise for his work with Jalen Hurts and did not play in Philadelphia's first preseason game, another sign of how the team views him. The Eagles traded a fifth-round pick and a 2027 sixth-rounder to Green Bay for Wicks in April, then extended him through 2027. He caught 30 of 46 targets for 332 yards and two touchdowns in 14 games last season, though he did post 581 yards and four scores as a rookie in 2023. Wicks now has a cleaner path to regular snaps than he ever had in Green Bay, giving him a path to fantasy relevance in deeper redraft leagues.
